Hi Rajesh / Emily,

Thanks again for the call this morning  good overview of FinTrust's use cases and the data sensitivity profile. Quick recap and a proposed set of next steps so we can scope the technical workshop: 

Key items from our discussion:
- PII/PHI surface: customer names, account numbers, transaction metadata  majority of workloads are inference-only (no model training).
- Data residency: primary region requirement is US (multi-region read replicas okay).
- Retention: logs and audit trails  FinTrust requires 2-year retention for break-glass/audit events.
- RBAC & least privilege: you want role-based access for product admins, analysts, and an explicit separate support role.
- Support access: must be time-limited, approved, auditable; prefer jumpbox + approval workflow; break-glass should be logged and alert security.

Proposed next steps:
1) Share any existing access matrix or policy (IAM roles)  that will help us map Redwood roles to your roles.
2) Technical workshop (60m) with your security lead + our infra engineer (Dev Patel) to walk RBAC & support access flows and demo break-glass audit logs.
3) Follow-up with a short runbook and a draft SLA language for support access.

Can you share the access matrix (CSV) and confirm availability for a workshop early next week? Ive proposed a few slots here: https://calendar.redwood.ai/event/abc123-tech-workshop

Thanks,

Rajesh  great, thanks for the attachments and clarifications. A few notes and how Redwood can meet each requirement: 

PII & data residency
- Redwood hosted: region pinning available (US-only), and Dedicated/Private deployment options if you need on-prem isolation.

Retention & audit logs
- Audit events (including support sessions and break-glass) are logged to our audit store. Default retention is 12 months on hosted but we offer configurable retention (24 months) as an enterprise add-on; logs are exportable in CSV/NDJSON for third-party archival.

RBAC & identity integration
- We support role-based roles (Admin, Operator, Analyst, Support) and granular permissions.
- SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning for mapping AD groups is supported  can sync your AD groups to Redwood roles.

Support access & break-glass
- Support access is implemented as time-bound, request-approved sessions. For Hosted, we provide temporary support tokens that are generated via an approval workflow and are fully audited.
- Break-glass flow: explicit ticket + approver, automatic generation of a high-fidelity audit event, and optional alerting to your security Slack/incident channel.

Attachments: Ive attached a short whitepaper that outlines our access-control model and recommended least-privilege mappings (redwood-access-controls-whitepaper.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm workshop time: Monday 2027-05-31 10:00 AM PST works for our team.
- Dev will demo role mappings + a short break-glass simulation.
- Ill follow up after the workshop with: runbook + a proposed support-access SLA paragraph that you can include in procurement.

Thanks  looking forward to a short, technical session.
